blocks.content: CCI can impose penalties up to 10% of a company's average turnover. In cartel cases, penalties may reach three times the profit.
In cartel cases, penalties may reach three times the profit.

items: Distinguish between standard penalty caps (up to 10% of average turnover) and cartel penalty caps (up to 3x profit).
Pay attention to the base metric: general penalties apply to 'average turnover', while cartel penalties are tied to 'profit'.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has statutory powers to levy heavy monetary penalties on defaulting companies.
The standard statutory cap for general penalties is set at 10% of a company's average turnover.
Cartel cases carry enhanced penalty limits, reaching up to three times the profit realized by the entity.
